So remember, in the rise phase, society is democratic and open but as you move on, it becomes more bureaucratic and ultimately authoritarian. We will see the United States and Europe become much more authoritarian; we're already seeing this happen in the United States where Trump is using more and more military to resolve issues.

As people have less and less right to speak up, they feel less invested in the system and are less willing to work, leading to economic collapse. People don't believe in the system anymore, and this will lead to immigration. The government might decide to bring in immigrants to do the work instead of letting the population continue to fight each other. This leads to civil conflict, which can escalate into civil war. Governments may send people off to stupid pointless wars overseas to distract them.

Europe and America will see less freedom and democracy, economic collapse, increased immigration, civil conflict, and ultimately stupid foreign wars. These events may happen in different orders but will occur concurrently.

The government might try to use a war to distract the people if they are dissatisfied with the system, as sending them to war is an effective way to avoid revolution. Power dynamics and the behavior of those in power are central themes in this analysis; there's no right or wrong, only how power works.

If these predictions come true, our model has some accuracy, but we must remain open to refining it based on new information. Understanding how the world works through this lens may help us build a more just world together.
